plan: My private value is $30. In a first-round auction with no prior history, rational bidders will likely bid strategically near their private value. The optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. If I bid too low, I risk losing the item. If I bid too high, I might pay more than the item's worth. A bid around $25-$28 seems optimal - close to my value but leaving room for potential profit.

With a private value of $7, I want to win only if the winning price is below my value. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders are likely to bid strategically around their own values. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to minimize potential losses. A bid around $6.5-$6.9 would allow me to potentially win while protecting against overpaying.

With a private value of $36, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the prize is worth $36 to me, I want to bid strategically. Given the $0-$49 range, other bidders likely have varied values. A safe strategy is to bid slightly below my true value, around $35, hoping to win if others bid conservatively. This allows potential profit if I win and minimizes loss if I overbid. The second-price auction mechanism incentivizes honest, near-true-value bidding.
